title: Two codebases. One application.
summary: Combining a supplied interface and application logic with persistent storage.
problem: The client had pieces from two separate repositories and needed them to work together as one project.
work: We connected the supplied interface and application logic into one C++ project, then added SQLite storage and clear setup instructions.
handoff: An integrated C++ project, database layer and setup guide.
boundary: Local C++/SQLite demonstration. No live payment connection.
caption: Architecture illustration of the integrated C++ application.

title: A training session people can follow.
summary: A staff-development presentation, with a presenter walkthrough.
problem: The client needed a presentation for training staff and help preparing to deliver it.
work: We created a staff-training presentation with clear learning goals, timed activities, discussion prompts and reflection. We also walked the client through the deck so they could prepare to lead the session.
boundary: Client identity withheld. The slide is an actual excerpt from our work.
caption: Slide from a staff-training presentation we created.

title: A place to see the work—and enquire.
summary: A construction-company website organised around projects and contact.
problem: The client wanted prospective customers to view construction work and get in touch.
work: We designed and developed a website that brings the company’s services and project portfolio together. Visitors can explore individual projects and find a clear route to get in touch.
handoff: Company website with project and service pages.
boundary: The showcase uses anonymous branding and recreated visuals to protect the client’s identity.
caption: Recreated website showcase with anonymous branding and original architectural illustrations.

title: Finance inside. A clear presence outside.
summary: A school finance tracker paired with a public-facing website.
problem: The client needed a way to track school finances and a website for public information.
work: We built a school finance tracker and a public-facing school website. The tracker brings fee management, donations, expenses and financial reporting into one interface.
handoff: Finance tracker and public-facing school website.
boundary: Review environment with sample data. School identity and financial records kept private.
caption: Our finance review dashboard, shown with sample data.

title: Books within reach.
summary: A digital library for teacher uploads and student reading.
problem: The client wanted teachers to upload PDF books so students could read remotely on different devices.
work: We built a digital library where teachers can upload PDF books and students can read online from different devices. The review site let us walk through the design with the client before their own deployment.
handoff: Digital-library platform for PDF upload and reading.
boundary: Public review site. Portfolio screenshots show the interface, not a client’s books or student records.
caption: Our digital-library review site. The client’s deployment remains private.

title: A consistent professional introduction.
summary: A CV, LinkedIn refresh and one-page bio for a job seeker.
problem: The client wanted a clearer professional profile while looking for work.
work: We refreshed the client’s CV and LinkedIn profile and created a one-page bio, bringing all three into a consistent professional presentation.
handoff: A refreshed CV, LinkedIn profile and one-page bio.
boundary: Names, personal contacts, photographs and employment details are withheld.
caption: Anonymised illustration of the CV, LinkedIn profile and one-page bio.

title: Making a technical argument readable.
summary: Research drafting and guidance on a technical literature review.
problem: A postgraduate client requested drafting support and research guidance for a technical paper.
work: We helped draft and structure a technical literature review, developing the argument and explaining the proposed framework alongside research guidance.
handoff: A research draft and guidance on developing the argument.
boundary: The unpublished manuscript and client identity remain private.
caption: Original illustration of the research-writing process.
